easy.def: To leave something and never come back.
examples: They abandoned the old house.
Do not abandon your pet.
The boat was abandoned.

more.def: To go away and leave someone or something behind for good.
examples: The family abandoned the old farm and moved to town.
The sailors abandoned the sinking ship.
She would never abandon her pet when she moved.
She has the ability to swim fast.
Birds have the ability to fly.
He has the ability to draw well.

more.def: The power or skill to do something.
examples: Dolphins have the ability to talk to each other with clicks.
Her ability to remember names surprised her new teacher.
A good swimmer needs strength and the ability to stay calm.

easy.def: Having the power or skill to do something.
examples: I am able to tie my shoes.
Are you able to swim?
He was able to lift the box.

more.def: Having the strength, skill or chance to do something.
examples: Birds are able to fly long distances.
I was not able to come because I was sick.
She was able to solve the riddle in two minutes.

easy.def: On a boat, train, plane or bus.
examples: All aboard!
The kids are aboard.
We went aboard the ship.

more.def: On or onto a ship, train, plane or bus.
examples: The passengers climbed aboard the ferry.
Welcome aboard, said the pilot.
The captain called for everyone to come aboard.
This book is about frogs.
Tell me about your day.
We talked about the trip.

more.def: On the subject of something, or having to do with it.
examples: We read a story about a boy who builds a boat.
The scientist gave a talk about volcanoes.
What are you thinking about?
It is about noon.
I have about five stickers.
She is about as tall as me.

more.def: Close to a number or amount, but not exact.
examples: The walk to the park takes about ten minutes.
About twenty children came to the picnic.
The pond is about three feet deep.
The bird is above the tree.
The clock is above the door.
Fly above the clouds.

more.def: At a higher place than something else.
examples: The plane flew above the clouds.
A picture hangs above the fireplace.
The moon rose above the hills.
The stars above are bright.
Look at the sky above.
See the picture above.

more.def: In or to a higher place.
examples: The clouds above turned dark.
Read the paragraph above.
Birds circled above.
The music stopped abruptly.
The bus stopped abruptly.
He left abruptly.

more.def: In a way that is sudden and surprising.
examples: The road ended abruptly at the edge of the cliff.
The bus stopped abruptly, and we all jerked forward.
She abruptly left the room.
Her absence was noticed.
The teacher marked his absence.
The absence was long.

more.def: A time when someone or something is not in a place where they should be.
examples: Her absence from school was noticed.
His absence from the team was a big loss.
In the absence of rain, the plants dried up.
It was an absolute mess.
I have absolute trust in her.
There was absolute silence.
The room was in absolute silence.
I have absolute trust in my best friend.
It was an absolute mess after the party.
I am absolutely sure.
The room was absolutely quiet.
It was absolutely delicious.
The soup was absolutely delicious.
I am absolutely certain that I locked the door.
The night was absolutely silent.
A sponge can absorb water.
The towel absorbs the water on the floor.
Dry dirt absorbs the rain.

more.def: To take in or soak up something, such as a liquid, heat, or light.
examples: Dark clothes absorb more heat from the sun than light clothes.
Plant roots absorb water from the soil.
Thick curtains absorbed most of the noise from the street.
The idea is absurd.
The joke was absurd.
He wore an absurd hat.

more.def: So silly that it makes no sense.
examples: The idea of a cat driving a car is absurd.
He wore an absurd hat with a feather.
The story was so absurd that we laughed.
